input: # A string written as adjacent literals, `"a" "b"`, wherever protoc reads
# a string (Parser::ConsumeString in protobuf's compiler/parser.cc): the
# declaration, every import, an option's value, default, json_name and a
# reserved name. protoc records ONE string, each literal decoded by its
# tokenizer (ParseStringAppend in io/tokenizer.cc) and the bytes run
# together, and so does this package; ts/src/strings.ts is that reading.
# A string written as ONE literal is recorded as written, as it always
# has been (see the root AGENTS.md). Adjacent literals protoc's tokenizer
# refuses, a backtick string or an escape it does not know, are refused.
# Every row was checked against protoc 36.2's own parser and agrees with
# an option's value, in every place an option is written
# default and json_name, which are not options; a bytes field's default is escaped again, as protoc does
# a reserved name, in a message and in an enum

# each literal is decoded as protoc decodes it, and the bytes concatenated: octal, hex and the letter escapes, \u and \U, a surrogate pair written as two \u escapes, UTF-8 as written, and a \U past U+10FFFF written out as text, as protoc writes it
# bytes that are not UTF-8 are recorded with U+FFFD for each ill-formed sequence: protoc keeps the bytes themselves, which JSON text cannot hold
# protoc refuses these: a sign before a string, and adjacent literals where its tokenizer refuses one, for an escape it does not know or a backtick string, at every site
